full_judgment: 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court in passing the impugned judgment and decree committed gross illegality and irregularity. In deciding the merit of the appeal there has been glaring misconception of law, misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties conclusively proved that the defendant's kabla deed which is prior to the plaintiffs was duly effected and possession was delivered by the vendor of the transfer deed in respect of 08 decimals of land from plot No. 9093 exclusively in which the defendant-petitioners after erecting their homestead and boundary wall possessing the same for more than thirty yearn openly and adversely within the knowledge of others. The area of the land as it appears from the concerned khatian that in plot No. 9093 the plaintiffs only obtained 05(five) decimals of land by their kabla deed from the defendant no.2 which is correctly decided by the trial court after proper assessment of evidence but the appellate P court below without rebutting the findings of the trial court in this regard adverting evidence on records reversed the judgment and decree which is gross illegality on the face of the record. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiffs after purchasing the land, constructed boundary wall and the appellate court failed to appreciate that aspect and thereby arrived at a wrong conclusion as to the quantum of land. The plaintiffs in the year 1970 after the defendant's purchased 07(seven) decimals of land from it plot Nos.9091 and 9093 subsequently obtained a deed of rectification with a mention that they have purchased the land only from plot No. 9093. The deed of rectification was not acted upon inasmuch as the defendant No.2 after the transfer in favour of the purchaser-defendants had no subsisting interest excepting 05(five) decimals of land in the aforesaid plot No.9093 which is properly evaluated by the trial court. The learned lower appellate court failed to appreciate the evidence on records 4 in its true perspective and without giving any cogent reason and rebutting the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of their total claim which is not in accordance with law and as such the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable.
